Title: xCatalog — Filter Combinator (AND vs OR) Is Part of the Dedup Cache Key, Not Just Member Values (VCST-5637)
Preconditions: Runner-native. PUBLIC role. Live-discovered two real single-valued Brand terms (3DR: 89 products, BROTHER: 1 product in this catalog, live-verified 2026-08-05) whose per-product cardinality makes AND (Brand: repeated as two separate terms) and OR (Brand: comma-joined values) mathematically distinguishable even though both reference the exact same two member values: AND must be the empty intersection (no product is simultaneously both brands); OR must be the union (sum of both single-brand counts). If catalog reseeding changes the specific counts, the relationship (and_combo=0, or_combo=b1+b2) still holds structurally — do not hardcode the counts themselves.
Assertions:
[ERRORS label=filter_combinator] errors[] empty
[DATA label=filter_combinator] data.b1.totalCount > 0
[DATA label=filter_combinator] data.and_combo.totalCount = 0
[DATA label=filter_combinator] data.or_combo.totalCount = data.b1.totalCount + data.b2.totalCount
Cross_Layer_Checks: [EVIDENCE] Live-verified 2026-08-05: b1=89, b2=1, and_combo=0, or_combo=90 (=89+1) — and_combo and or_combo reference the identical two brand values yet resolve to different totals, proving the dedup cache key is combinator-aware. A value-only hash (ignoring AndFilter vs OrFilter shape) would risk collapsing these two distinct requests onto one cached slice, silently returning 90 for the AND case or 0 for the OR case.
Failure_Signals: errors[] non-empty; and_combo.totalCount != 0 (AND semantics broken, or the OR-combo's cached slice leaked into the AND-combo's response); or_combo.totalCount != b1+b2 (OR semantics broken, or the AND-combo's cached 0 leaked into the OR-combo's response); DV-008 on Brand filter syntax
References: VCST-5637; PROPOSED-BL-GQL-005; xAPI; Query.products filter DSL; Promoted: VCST-5637 (2026-08-05)
